item.title: Definitely no or maybe yes: what tipped the Icelandic referendum | Miranda Bryant
item.description: The no campaign was well-funded and accused of scaremongering, but the wording of the question may also have made a difference It was always going to be a close contest. But on the night, the figures showed just how divided Iceland was on the issue of whether or not to restart negotiations with the European Union. After a nail-biting overnight count, the well-funded no campaign rejoiced on Sunday morning as the broadcaster RUV declared it the winner with about 52.8% of the vote. item.title: A lone Black woman’s defiance of Swedish neo-Nazis, 10 years on
